recipes.name: Homemade Tomato Basil Pasta Sauce
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat; cook the tomatoes in the melted butter until they begin to fall apart, 5 to 7 minutes. Add the basil, olive oil, garlic salt, salt, and pepper. Slowly stir the flour into the mixture and cook until it begins to thicken, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir the water through the mixture to break up any lumps of the flour. Mix the garlic into the sauce and simmer another 5 minutes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Tomato Basil Pasta Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Fresh tomatoes and basil are quickly simmered with garlic to make a tasty pasta sauce.

review.reviewBody: Excellent basic sauce recipe. Easy to prepare great flavor. Substituted red wine for the water. This sauce is full of flavor and coats the pasta evenly. Will be adding this one to the regular rotation. You should definitely try this one.

Delicious! I was concerned at first, but it turned out lovely. Here's some hints I found useful: if using dried instead of fresh basil, use only four teaspoons. I also found that I didn't need the 1/4 cup water, and added used two tablespoons whole wheat flour rather than one all purpose. Also, you can just use a 28 oz can of diced tomatoes, and if you want to save some calories, only use one teaspoon margarine rather than a tablespoon butter, and omit the oil. It will still taste great.

Doubled the recipe and used wine instead of water. No flour added small can tomato paste. 1 tsp Italian seasoning. Didn't have fresh basil so used idea of 4 tsp dried basil from another reviewer. Sauteed fresh mushrooms and added them along with both onion powder and garlic powder. Simmered while meatballs baked. Turned out great. Lots of flavor. Very easy.

Excellent recipe. I used eight small tomatoes picked fresh from the garden and put them in a food processor. Instead of 1/4 cup water I used an 1/8 cup wine and an 1/8 cup water. I did not use flour but simmered the sauce for 30 minutes. Perfection. The basil and fresh tomatoes were superb.

For a first-time sauce maker (me) this was an excellent starter recipe. I did deviate a bit based on our tastes- doubled the fresh basil, doubled the minced garlic, added onion and oregano (about 2 tsp dried) and used sea salt instead of garlic salt. After cooking, I pureed it - also added a pinch of sugar. So while I changed it quite a bit- this was an excellent base and quick to make!

This recipe was simple and delicious and the perfect way to use up the tomatoes from my garden. I followed the recipe with the exception of the water. I used white wine instead and it came out very tasty. I also sauteed about 4 cloves of minced garlic in the butter, then added the tomatoes. I also added sea salt and a little sugar instead of the garlic salt. I can't want to make this again, next time with more tomatoes!

Yummy! So easy and so much better than store bought. I didn’t have fresh tomatoes so I used two cans of diced tomatoes per another suggestion. I also added oregano, Italian seasoning, additional garlic, and a few dashes of cayenne for a bit of kick. Blended it with the stick blender to smooth it out and voilà…delicious!

UPDATE JUNE 22, 2011: I made this sauce again for lunch without the flour and water and it was delicious. My 2 and 3 year old boys devoured their pasta and had second helpings. This makes for a great quick sauce that can be cooked up as the pasta is cooking. JUNE 20, 2011: I would like to give this sauce more points but I feel that it only deserves 3 points. After adding the flour, it made the tomato sauce really pasty and gooey. The preferred method to thicken up tomato sauce is to let it reduce rapidly over high heat, or slowly over medium/low heat, to the desired consistancy. This sauce is perfect without the addition of flour and water at the end. The other change I made was adding garlic powder and salt to taste because I had no garlic salt. I will make this again but omiting the flour and water at the end. Just add the minced garlic along with the olive oil and basil and cook accordingly.

This was ahh-mazing!! I did change it a bit! First I didn't have as many tomatoes as needed so I used a can of crushed tomatoes and one regular tomato. I also added chopped garlic and onions in the beginning with the tomatoes. I did everything as stated but didn't have fresh basil on hand so used 4 teaspoons dried (as mentioned by another user)! I also added the flour and didn't feel the need for the water! It was seriously so delish that my roommates raved, and I couldn't stop eating!
Second time I make this sauce and is fantastic! Followed the recipe almost exactly, just changed water for wine.
So good! Pureed afterwards and used as lasagna sauce.
Good and easy. Added onion and used wine instead of water per reviews. Served on rotini with sautéed prima vera veggies.
This makes for an easy meal in the cold months that will please everyone. You can really taste the summer. This recipe really lets the flavor of garden tomatoes shine.
I added more garlic, zucchini, onion and Parmesan cheese. Did not use the flour

I liked the recipe, but I made enough changes that I’m not sure whether it’s a fair review. Like many people, I substituted wine for the water. I put perhaps 1 teaspoon of flour again before stopping. I added a tablespoon of oregano, once more based on something someone else said. I tripled the amount of garlic, but I am minced it finally rather than grading it. I had arugula left from another recipe, so I put it in at the very end. My husband said that he felt like it needed something else, but since he’s not a cook, he couldn’t tell me what. If I make it again, I will have to include chicken.
Delicious! I added onion and spinach. So yummy and easy!
I love pasta and sauce so much. So easy for a quick dinner.

Made it twice . No changes.
LOVED IT. Great flavor.
No changes, just went a little more on the basil, garlic and butter.
Final test is with grandkids!
Stay tuned.
Great base recipe! Quick, easy, but I did make some tweaks for the meatballs I added to it. Substituted white wine for the water, added some oregano, and doubled the garlic. I love garlic!
